vocabulary.meaning_en: no longer needed for a job, so you lose it
vocabulary.meaning_ar: مُستغنى عنه (فائض عن الحاجة في العمل)
vocabulary.note_ar: make someone redundant = يستغني عن موظف لعدم الحاجة إلى وظيفته.
vocabulary.note_en: Make someone redundant = end their job because it's not needed.
vocabulary.example: Fifty workers were made redundant.

vocabulary.meaning_en: losing your job because your job is no longer needed
vocabulary.example: Many staff are facing redundancy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to be in danger of losing your job
vocabulary.example: I never thought I would be facing redundancy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (polite) to end someone's job
vocabulary.note_ar: أسلوب ألطف من sack أو fire.
vocabulary.example: I'm afraid we have to let you go.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) to end someone's job; get the sack = lose your job
vocabulary.example: He got the sack for being rude to customers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) to lose your job
vocabulary.example: I hope I don't get the chop.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (formal) to end something officially
vocabulary.example: The company terminated his contract.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having a paid job
vocabulary.example: Your employment will end on Friday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person or company that pays people to work
vocabulary.example: My employer pays me every month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who works for a company
vocabulary.example: The company has 200 employees.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a warning that a job will end after a set time
vocabulary.note_en: Notice period = the time between the warning and the end.
vocabulary.example: He gave me seven days' notice.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the time between being told your job will end and the last day
vocabulary.example: My notice period is one month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to change the way a company is organised
vocabulary.example: The company is restructuring its sales team.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (euphemism) to restructure or change a business
vocabulary.meaning_ar: يعيد ترتيب الأمور (تعبير ملطّف عن إعادة الهيكلة)
vocabulary.note_ar: تعبير ملطّف، لا علاقة له بالأثاث الحقيقي.
vocabulary.example: We've got to move the furniture around.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to have enough money to pay for something
vocabulary.example: We can't afford a new office.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person's job or position
vocabulary.example: My role is no longer needed.

vocabulary.meaning_en: difficult
vocabulary.example: It's a tough economic situation.

vocabulary.meaning_en: showing you understand and care about someone's problem
vocabulary.example: Be sympathetic when a colleague is upset.

vocabulary.meaning_en: someone who listens and comforts you
vocabulary.example: She was a shoulder to cry on when I lost my job.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make someone feel happier
vocabulary.meaning_ar: يُدخل البهجة على شخص / يرفع معنوياته
vocabulary.example: Let's buy her flowers to cheer her up.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to tell someone bad news
vocabulary.example: How will he break the news to the team?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to empty your desk because you are leaving
vocabulary.example: She cleared out her desk on her last day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an office tool that joins papers with small metal pins
vocabulary.example: Can I borrow your stapler?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small pad of paper for writing notes
vocabulary.example: Bring a notepad to the meeting.

fine_lines.title: employer vs employee
fine_lines.explanation_ar: employer صاحب العمل الذي يدفع الراتب. employee الموظف الذي يعمل ويتقاضى الراتب. لاحظ النهاية: er-ـ للذي يُوظِّف، و ee-ـ للذي يُوظَّف.
fine_lines.explanation_en: The employer gives the job and pays. The employee does the job. -er = the one who does it, -ee = the one it is done to.

examples.sentence: My employer gave me a laptop.

fine_lines.title: let go vs sack vs make redundant
fine_lines.explanation_ar: let someone go أسلوب مهذب لإنهاء العمل. sack عامية وتُستخدم غالبًا عند الطرد بسبب خطأ. make redundant تعني أن الوظيفة نفسها لم تعد ضرورية، وليس خطأ الموظف.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Let go' is polite. 'Sack' is informal, often for bad behaviour. 'Make redundant' means the job is not needed – it's not the worker's fault.

examples.sentence: I'm afraid we have to let you go.
Ten people were made redundant when the factory closed.

expressions.phrase: We've got to move the furniture around.
expressions.meaning_ar: علينا أن نعيد ترتيب الأمور (إعادة هيكلة).
expressions.meaning_en: We need to restructure the business.
expressions.example: Business is slow, so we've got to move the furniture around.

expressions.phrase: I'm afraid I've got to let you go.
expressions.meaning_en: I'm sorry, but your job is ending.
expressions.example: I'm afraid I've got to let you go. It's not about your work.

expressions.phrase: I'm giving you seven days' notice.
expressions.meaning_en: Your job will end in seven days.
expressions.example: I'm giving you one month's notice.

expressions.phrase: I'm really sorry to hear this.
expressions.meaning_en: A kind reply to bad news.
expressions.example: You lost your job? I'm really sorry to hear this.

expressions.phrase: My role is no longer needed.
expressions.meaning_ar: لم يعد هناك حاجة إلى منصبي.
expressions.meaning_en: My job is not necessary any more.
expressions.example: The company bought a machine, so my role is no longer needed.

expressions.phrase: Could I have a word with you in my office, please?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكنني التحدث معك في مكتبي من فضلك؟
expressions.meaning_en: I want to talk to you privately.
expressions.example: Denise, could I have a word with you in my office, please?

expressions.meaning_en: Try to look at the good side.
expressions.example: It's hard, but you've got to think positively.

grammar.title: I'm afraid + bad news (softening)
grammar.explanation_ar: نبدأ بـ I'm afraid لتلطيف خبر سيئ أو رفض بطريقة مهذبة. لا تعني هنا «أنا خائف»، بل «يؤسفني».
grammar.explanation_en: Start with 'I'm afraid' to give bad news politely. It means 'I'm sorry to say', not 'I'm scared'.
examples: I'm afraid I've got to let you go.
I'm afraid the manager is busy.
I'm afraid we can't accept your offer.

grammar.title: have got to = must
grammar.explanation_ar: have got to + الفعل الأساسي تعني «يجب»، وهي شائعة في الإنجليزية البريطانية المنطوقة: I've got to = I have to.
grammar.explanation_en: 'Have got to' means 'have to / must', common in spoken British English.
examples: We've got to move the furniture around.
I've got to let you go.

grammar.title: Possessive with time: seven days' notice
grammar.explanation_ar: مع المدد الزمنية نستخدم الملكية: one week's notice، two weeks' notice (الفاصلة العليا بعد s في الجمع).
grammar.explanation_en: Use the possessive with periods of time: one week's, seven days'.
examples: I'm giving you seven days' notice.
We'll deliver in two weeks' time.

questions.question: 'I'm afraid I've got to let you go' means ___.
questions.explanation_ar: let you go تعني إنهاء عملك بأسلوب مهذب.
questions.explanation_en: It politely means your job is ending.

questions.question: If a boss says 'We've got to move the furniture around', he means ___.
questions.explanation_en: It's a soft way to say restructure.

questions.question: I'm giving you seven ___ notice.
questions.explanation_ar: مع الجمع نضع الفاصلة العليا بعد s: seven days'.

questions.question: The person who pays you to work is your ___.
Which phrase is the most informal?
Anna tells Tom to be more ___ to Denise.
A 'notice period' is ___.
choices: the time between being told your job ends and your last day
questions.explanation_en: It's the time before your job ends.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: I'm afraid we can't to keep you.
I afraid we can't keep you.
I'm afraid we can't keep you.
I'm afraid we not keep you.
questions.explanation_ar: I'm afraid + جملة صحيحة: can't + الفعل الأساسي.

questions.question: Denise needs 'a shoulder to cry on'. She needs ___.
'We can't ___ to keep everyone' means we don't have enough money.
